summary: Every test case's process status in cpu-sec-bench was made a declared, deterministic contract value. The cycle added lib/include/result.hpp as the single home of the RT_CODE_* family and the confirmed R1 vocabulary: 0 for a successful attack; one shared 1 meaning the attack was launched with no platform signal, deliberately not saying whether a silent defense stopped it; case-local 2-14 declared per record in configure.json expect-results with meanings; a 15-31 caught-exception-and-library band comprising the memory faults 15 and 16, the mismatch diagnostic 19 that is never declared, the library-failure 20 and the contained-fault 21; the retained 32-63 and 64-65 runtime-parameter channels; and the two named out-of-band exceptions 99 and 251. Both platform signal layers now include that header and define no result constant of their own, and the POSIX handler's 2023 regression was repaired — its guard exit moved inside the predicate, deliveries switched to write plus _exit, the registration pool bounded, SA_EXPOSE_TAGBITS installed under an EINVAL retry with tagged addresses normalized — with the Windows port brought to parity. The method was enumeration-first: a tester-built table over every delivery site in the case sources and the support library pinned the vocabulary before any source edit, and acceptance was read on a per-run measure across both scheduler legs from a cleaned variables.json, which is what exposed the pre-existing raw-sweep argument spaces and the undeclared crash classes that per-record results had hidden; the per-case edits changed only how the status is delivered, never an attack's mechanism. Design decisions worth carrying forward: the scheduler was left untouched because it encodes only the parameter, temp-file, 1024/1025 and 256-plus-signo bands, so the 0-31 contract lives in the header and the documentation rewrites of README, doc/architecture.html, doc/porting.html and CLAUDE.md were made together with it under a documented contract amendment; and two pre-existing registry or case defects that the cycle's own instruments surfaced — the eight enclosing-array-pointer large-count records sweeping one value past their table, and the sibling write case's unguarded selector — were fixed rather than declared as platform outcomes. A post-finalize step then retired the catalog guard's two obsolete count legs, the CLAUDE.md exact-count phrase and the doc/content.html figure table, and genericized the landing page under the user's exact-count ruling. Four issues stay open as machine-local deferrals — the four mss sources with a bare int rv, the nonalloc redzone distance written before its match, the four dangling require names that make fast-run exit 1, and the two platform defects delivered from the environment repository's outbox — and the environment successor cycle owns the BENCH_COMMIT bump, the all-lane re-run at the new pin and the CHERI and riscv64 riders.

The benchmark could only run on native hosts, because the scheduler compiles each variant of each test case at run time, while the target venue - a booted Linux guest under XiangShan NEMU - has no compiler, no writable network and a transient initramfs, so the suite needed a build-elsewhere run-here split plus a platform that fabricates a bootable image containing the prebuilt corpus. The core bench change is a new corpus option in scheduler/run-test.cpp: the build phase always forces -B and snapshots each freshly built unit as test/<program>__<key>, where the key is a deterministic FNV-1a-32 over the record's macro map rendered as sorted comma-joined K=V pairs (empty map 811c9dc5), and the run phase executes that keyed path and fails fast naming the file when it is missing; the snapshot is what keeps the seventeen multi-variant programs honest, since a plain make-only/no-make split would run whichever variant happened to be built last, and non-corpus behaviour is strictly unchanged. The new platform/riscv64-nemu-linux venue cross-builds that corpus with the environment repository's riscv64-lane toolchain pins, stages it together with the riscv64 scheduler and the NEEDED and PT_INTERP library closure resolved through the cross compiler, gates the staged tree on an independent manifest check, assembles a NEMU image from pinned inputs (workload-builder, OpenSBI v1.9, LibCheckpointAlpha, Linux 6.18.56 and busybox 1.36.1, both tarballs sha256-pinned) with a guest overlay that mounts /proc and /sys and hands its exit code to NEMU through the nemu trap instruction, and boots it under a host timeout with the result files carved out of the console log between markers; a companion native runner produces the distribution the guest run is compared against. The load-bearing deviation was the guest kernel: the pinned cross toolchain's glibc executes RISC-V vector instructions unconditionally while kernels before 6.5 have no userspace vector support, so 6.1.83 made every guest process die with SIGILL on its first vector instruction, and the pin moved to 6.18.56 with CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_V and CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_V_DEFAULT_ENABLE asserted against the built config, ratified by the plan owner after a XiangShan-side audit found no kernel-version pin. Verification ran as two tester rounds plus a Phase 6 adversarial review whose four Warning findings - per-class runsets aborting at staging, a manifest collision check that could never fail, host build legs inheriting an exported cross toolchain, and a run harness that accepted an aborted guest as success - were fixed and independently re-verified in a third round: the full image boots to 246 of 246 records with HIT GOOD TRAP and agrees with the host-native reference on 244 of them, both differing records traced with neither caused by this plan, both runsets' images are byte-reproducible, and an independent corpus rebuild reproduces the staged tree byte for byte. Two hazards stay open as deferrals for the successor cycle, which also integrates this platform as a cpu-sec-test-env lane: the registry swap the corpus builder performs is crash-unsafe under a hard kill and carries no lock, and the canonical rendering is not injective for a value containing a comma-key fragment.

Pinning the environment's lane sweep to cpu-sec-bench commit c8c6000 exposed two latent defects in the acc-read-func opcode-extraction path that the pin's own hardening had turned from silent misbehaviour into hard failures: the extractor scripts called bare objdump and so resolved it through PATH, where on the four aarch64 lanes the host x86_64 objdump could not decode the cross-architecture binaries and the case became a build failure recorded as 1025, and the Makefile's extractor selection knew only aarch64 and riscv64, so the cheri_riscv64 port fell back to the x64 extractor against an xcheri binary and aborted the corpus build. The fix makes the extraction consume the OBJDUMP knob the bench already publishes - the side-file rule passes it into the extractor invocation, the three cross-target scripts require it explicitly and fail loudly when it is unset, since a PATH-resolved objdump on those targets is the host's own tool - and gives cheri_riscv64 its own branch plus a new CHERI-capable extractor script, selected on the effective ARCH because enable_riscv64_cheri forces ARCH later in the Makefile's parse order. The Step 2 decision gate resolved to a genuine CHERI extraction rather than a declared skip, because the alternative would have flipped the case's declared 290 capability-fault verdict into a 2 report of a failed extraction. All four POSIX extractors now run every objdump call through a bounded runner, check the tool's exit status before parsing, name the resolved tool in their hard errors, echo an audit line carrying the resolved tool and its version, and assert the extracted word's exact width and hex shape before writing the side file; acc/read-func.cpp adds a side-file parse check so an unparseable or empty file can never be masked as the declared defense, plus a missing-argument guard, neither changing the result-code contract. The declared boundaries: CHERI's run-time verdict does not depend on the side-file value, so correctness there is carried at extraction time by the width assertion and an independent recomputation; a stock macOS without timeout falls back to an unbounded objdump call; the Windows/MSVC half of the pass-through is deferred for lack of a test path; and real-lane confirmation of the four aarch64 lanes and the cheri lane belongs to the successor environment cycle, which after its re-run at this commit also retires the two env-filed deferrals this plan deliberately holds open.

Seven deferred issues were cleared in one bench-side sweep of cpu-sec-bench: the run-test continue path's variables.json load was retargeted from the result database to the variable database and the JSON reader hardened so malformed input exits 1; eight pre-existing scheduler compiler warnings were cleared behavior-preservingly; script/check_catalog.py was hardened to assert the published count figures against registry-derived values and to fail on unclosed or duplicate classed cells with exit 2 on malformed input; the function-opcode extraction scripts gained an exact symbol-column anchor with an exactly-one-address assertion and address-span disassembly selection honoring the documented func_name, fixing the riscv64 acc-read-func regression caused by the translated assembly_helper symbol; and .size directives were added to all five independent-assembly sources, clearing the CHERI linker's unsized-capability-relocation warning. The plan also classified the 29 handoff verdict rows from the environment plan's CHERI and Morello lane runs into a decision table, and on the user's confirmation declared 290 on the six distinct SIGPROT records and 1 on mss-write-by-stack-pointer while leaving 267 undeclared on corrupted-frame evidence and routing the 255 fakefunc sentinel and the fourteen generic-code rows to a separate return-code-delivery plan. The chief trade-offs: no test-case source was touched, no real-lane run happened bench-side (the environment successor's pin-bump re-run confirms on lanes), and two issues remain open as deferrals, argv-conv-bounds and testcase-return-code-delivery. Files changed are scheduler/run-test.cpp, the three extraction scripts, script/check_catalog.py, five lib indepassembly sources, configure.json, CLAUDE.md and doc/architecture.html.

The bench's per-platform flag blocks are meant to make a configuration self-sufficient apart from the compiler choice, and the Morello block already carried its FreeBSD target triple on the C++ and object lines plus an ASMFLAGS line, but enable_riscv64_cheri carried neither a --target nor any ASMFLAGS: with a caller-supplied CTSRD clang++ the C++ path failed on -mabi=l64pc128d and the assembler defaulted to the host triple, so the independent-assembly source could not be assembled. The fix mirrors the Morello precedent: --target=riscv64-unknown-freebsd is prepended to CXXFLAGS and OBJECT_CXXFLAGS, and ASMFLAGS gains the triple, -march=rv64gcxcheri and -mabi=l64pc128d, while SCHEDULER_CXXFLAGS stays host-only so the scheduler remains a host binary. Verification covers the Makefile block line by line and through the makefile's own rules, a real object build that yields a RISC-V FreeBSD ELF defining assembly_helper and assembly_return_site, and the first link-stage exercise of the translated asmfunc units with caller-supplied toolchain paths only; the full 246-record suite is byte-identical to the x86_64 reference and the catalog guard stays green. doc/porting.html was synced to the new contract, including the pre-existing Makefile ARCH evaluation quirk that keeps ARCH=cheri_riscv64 on the make line. Two pre-existing findings are deferred rather than fixed: the CHERI linker warning about the unsized capability relocation for assembly_return_site (lib/ was out of scope), and the cross-repo registry expectation gaps already tracked by the env repository's deferral. The fix commit must be pushed before the environment plan can pin BENCH_COMMIT to it.

cpu-sec-bench's riscv64, aarch64 and cheri_riscv64 ports had been unbuildable since November 2024, because assembly_return_site in each lib/<ARCH>/indepassembly.asm carried the untranslated x86-64 body copy-pasted from the x86 file, and the independent-assembly object is linked into every test binary. This plan translates that symbol per architecture from previously probe-verified texts, leaving the neighbouring assembly_helper bodies untouched, and adds the Morello purecap variant the dialect probe exposed: under enable_aarch64_morello the configuration is purecap, where the plain AArch64 bodies are rejected, so a new lib/aarch64/indepassembly_morello.asm supplies stp/ldp c29,c30 capability-frame bodies selected by the Makefile's independent_assembly definition, mirroring the existing MSVC variant precedent. Enabling that path also required completing the Morello flag set with the mandatory --target=aarch64-unknown-freebsd triple on CXXFLAGS, OBJECT_CXXFLAGS and a new ASMFLAGS line; without it every documented Morello invocation was unbuildable while all dry-run checks stayed green, which was the audit's High finding. The chief trade-offs: verification is natively and at object level only, since in-guest cross-arch execution waits on the successor environment plan (skip-injection removal, BENCH_COMMIT bump, lane re-runs) and on the C1 CHERI bring-up, and the deferral indepassembly-return-site-untranslated is retired bench-side while its env-side copy and workarounds remain.

cpu-sec-bench's scheduler could not distinguish a case it never ran - one deliberately unrunnable on the current platform, or one whose build failed - from a genuine test outcome, because a failed build recorded make's raw exit status as the case's result. This plan adds a scheduler-owned result code 1025 meaning not run, a per-record skip and skip-reason declaration matched against a CSB_TARGET_ARCH define the Makefile passes from ARCH after its feature-forcing blocks, a make-status sub-field in results.json carrying the raw build status, and two count lines in results.dat that report skipped and unbuildable records separately so lost coverage is never silent. It also adds a disable_independent_assembly build switch so a port can come up before its independent-assembly source is translated, and repairs two pre-existing defects the work surfaced: report_gen's sys-info header copy could loop forever and fill the disk, and cfi/return-to-peer-vfunc.cpp was missing the include that current g++ requires for uintptr_t. Files changed are scheduler/run-test.cpp, the Makefile, that one test-case source, and the README, doc/architecture.html, doc/porting.html and CLAUDE.md documentation set. The chief trade-off is that no skip declarations ship in configure.json: the mechanism is exercised through scratch registries, and the affected architectures stay covered by the opt-out plus automatic build-failure recording until the independent-assembly translation is finished.

Initialized Claude tooling, a browsable HTML documentation tree and repo hygiene for the public cpu-sec-bench repository, which previously had no CLAUDE.md, no working area and no browsable docs. The plan created a root CLAUDE.md guide covering rules, structure, commands and scheduler architecture; a declaration of the audit-relevant planner-owned locations at .claude/mega-audit-files.json; and a five-file doc/ tree holding a landing page, an architecture page documenting the scheduler algorithm, the configure.json field set and the nine-group exit-code contract, a curated catalog of all 246 records over 103 programs, a porting guide and a shared stylesheet. The catalog is guarded by a committed two-way set-equality check, script/check_catalog.py, chosen over generating the page from configure.json so that no generator or build step is added; it was renamed from check_test_catalog.py after that basename collided with a coder deny rule. Repo hygiene: .gitignore now ignores /tmp/, /.codegraph/ and /trace-log/ so machine-local working directories can never be committed, and the Makefile's dead LaTeX-era doc target was removed. README.md gained doc and plans entries plus the previously missing 64-65 result-code row, while INTERNAL.md's factual drift was declared and left unfixed as out of scope. Three issues remain deferred: the run-test continue variables.json defect, eight pre-existing scheduler compiler warnings, and hardening of the catalog guard.
